# Wyrd

> Wyrd is open-source AI assurance and verification infrastructure. Verify AI systems before and after release, with verdicts you can trace, reproduce, and audit.

## Start here

Set up a local server, then run one verification, in this order. A connected Wyrd MCP server teaches the same route through `wyrd.guide {"topic":"start"}`.

- [Set up Wyrd](/wyrd/get-started/setup/): install Wyrd and start a local server you keep running.
- [Run your first verification](/wyrd/get-started/quickstart/): declare a Verifier in YAML and verify a passing and a failing support answer from Python, Rust, or TypeScript.

## Home

- [Wyrd docs](/wyrd/): the docs home, with a link to each published section.

## Get started

- [What Wyrd does](/wyrd/get-started/introduction/): Wyrd verifies what your AI system does against the requirements you declare, and records which versions produced each result.
- [Set up Wyrd](/wyrd/get-started/setup/): Install the Wyrd 0.3.0 CLI and SDK for Python, Rust, or TypeScript, then let your coding agent start a local server and run a first verification, or do it by hand.
- [Run your first verification](/wyrd/get-started/quickstart/): Declare a Verifier and the Service it checks in two YAML files, then verify a passing and a failing support answer from one Python, Rust, or TypeScript program.
- [Use with your coding agent](/wyrd/get-started/use-with-your-coding-agent/): Give your coding agent the Wyrd docs through llms.txt and Wyrd's tools through MCP with wyrd mcp install.

## Build and verify

- [Recipes](/wyrd/build-and-verify/verify/verifier-recipes/): Copyable Verifiers for common checks, each with its YAML and the Python that calls it - assertions, traces, Python checks, model judges, multi-step, grouped sessions, and drift.

## Connect

- [ASGI apps](/wyrd/connect/integrate-asgi/): Add WyrdMiddleware to a FastAPI, Starlette, Django, or Litestar app to start Wyrd with the app, verify inside one Run per request, and drain queued evidence at shutdown.

## Operate

- [Verification runtime](/wyrd/operate/configure-verification-runtime/): Choose which processes run Verifiers, size the worker pool, and diagnose startup refusals.

## Understand

- [Architecture](/wyrd/understand/architecture/): What a team deployment of Wyrd runs, what it connects to, and why each part is separate.
- [How verification works](/wyrd/understand/how-verification-works/): Inputs, steps, requirements, and decide; verify versus submit; executions, verdicts, results, and Operators.
- [Runs and evidence](/wyrd/understand/runs-observations-and-evidence/): How Wyrd records what a declared service actually does, and ties each observation to the version that ran.
- [Cards and versions](/wyrd/understand/cards-versions-and-relationships/): A Service declaration is a set of versioned Cards, each one a declared component of an AI system.
- [Bifrost](/wyrd/understand/bifrost/): Wyrd's analytical warehouse, the two ways to write to it, and when a written row becomes queryable.
- [Identity and access](/wyrd/understand/identity-and-authorization/): Every call to Wyrd is made as a principal whose roles decide what it may do, and every decision is audited.

## Reference

- [Verifier Card](/wyrd/reference/verifier-card/): Fields, input slots, steps, checks, operators, references, citations, and refusals of a Verifier spec.
- [Extraction output](/wyrd/reference/extraction-output/): The JSON an extract step returns for each media format.
- [Agent tools](/wyrd/reference/agent-tools-and-authorization/): Built-in tools a Verifier's Agent can call and the permissions each call needs.
- [Runtime limits](/wyrd/reference/verification-runtime-limits/): Environment settings that bound Verifier files, extraction, workspaces, and Python code, with defaults and startup rules.
- [MCP tools](/wyrd/reference/mcp-tools/): Wyrd MCP tool names, permissions, shapes, and query limits.
- [Error codes](/wyrd/api/errors/): Every stable Wyrd error code with its HTTP status, title, and fix.
- [HTTP API](/wyrd/api/openapi/): Where a Wyrd server serves its OpenAPI document and how to use it.

## Machine-readable reference

- [llms-full.txt](/wyrd/llms-full.txt): every page below in full, with its embedded YAML and code.
